candidate.answerReason: The probability that all three shiny pennies occur within the first four draws is 4/35. Its complement is 31/35 in lowest terms, so a+b=66.

methods.label: Method 1: Choose the shiny positions
methods.explanation:
The third shiny penny appears after draw 4 exactly when the first four draws do not contain all three shiny pennies. It is easier to count the complementary event.

Imagine drawing all seven pennies. The three positions occupied by shiny pennies form a set of three positions among seven. These sets are equally likely: if the pennies are temporarily distinguished, every complete ordering is equally likely, and each specified set of shiny positions allows the same number of orders within the shiny and dull groups.

There are
\[
\binom73=\frac{7\cdot6\cdot5}{3\cdot2\cdot1}=35
\]
possible shiny-position sets. All three shiny pennies appear within four draws in exactly
\[
\binom43=4
\]
of them. Each ordering determines exactly one such set, so the count has neither omissions nor repetitions. The desired probability is therefore
\[
1-\frac4{35}=\frac{31}{35}.
\]
Since 31 and 35 have no common factor greater than 1, this fraction is in lowest terms. Thus \(a+b=31+35=\boxed{66}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: This is a finite equally likely probability calculation using combinations and a complementary event.

methods.label: Method 2: Calculate the four early-finish patterns
methods.explanation:
To finish collecting the three shiny pennies within four draws, the first four draws must contain three shiny pennies and one dull penny. Write \(S\) for shiny and \(D\) for dull. The possible patterns are
\[
SSSD,\quad SSDS,\quad SDSS,\quad DSSS.
\]
These four patterns are disjoint and exhaust the complementary event, since the single dull draw can occupy any one of the four positions.

Because the pennies are not replaced, the total numbers available at the successive draws are 7, 6, 5, and 4. In any listed pattern, the shiny draws have respectively 3, 2, and 1 shiny pennies available, and the single dull draw has 4 dull pennies available. Multiplying the successive conditional probabilities therefore gives the same probability for every pattern:
\[
\frac{3\cdot2\cdot1\cdot4}{7\cdot6\cdot5\cdot4}
=\frac1{35}.
\]
Adding the four disjoint probabilities, the chance of finishing within four draws is \(\tfrac4{35}\). Consequently the chance of needing more than four draws is
\[
1-\frac4{35}=\frac{31}{35}.
\]
This is in lowest terms because 31 and 35 have no common factor greater than 1. Hence \(a+b=\boxed{66}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The alternative uses elementary draw-by-draw conditional probabilities and addition of four disjoint cases.

Combinations belong to the position-counting route; conditional multiplication and disjoint probability addition belong to the sequential route.
